tours.title: A conversation that remembers
tours.summary: Start with a complete question, use a pronoun, then ask for more without repeating the subject.
tours.presenterNote: Explain the difference between the persistent subject and the changing aspect. The trace shows where each inherited word came from.

steps.title: Establish the subject
steps.query: What is the James Webb Space Telescope?
steps.observe: The workspace creates a telescope topic and retrieves real Wikipedia passages.

steps.title: Ask a contextual follow-up
steps.observe: The telescope stays active while the focus changes to its mirror.

steps.title: Use an elliptical request
steps.observe: Open Query terms: the earlier mirror aspect is carried with its source turn.

tours.title: Switch topics. Return without mixing them.
tours.summary: Move from space exploration to gene editing, then resume the original conversation.
tours.presenterNote: Point to the two topic branches. Returning should reuse the original branch, not create a third one or carry CRISPR into telescope search.

steps.title: Start with the telescope
steps.observe: A telescope branch appears.

steps.title: Continue that branch
steps.observe: The pronoun resolves using the active telescope topic.

steps.title: Introduce a different subject
steps.observe: CRISPR becomes a separate branch; telescope memory remains available.

steps.title: Resume the first topic
steps.query: Back to JWST, what instruments does it carry?
steps.observe: The decision reads Resume topic and the original telescope branch becomes active.

tours.title: One word, two meanings
tours.summary: Resolve Mercury into a specific indexed meaning and preserve that choice in follow-ups.
tours.presenterNote: The interpretation choices come from the corpus. Selecting the element supplies additional user information; this is not an automatic fact-checking verdict.

steps.title: Ask an ambiguous question
steps.observe: The system offers the planet and chemical element instead of committing a guess.

steps.title: Choose the chemical element
steps.observe: The selected interpretation becomes the topic and changes the retrieved evidence.

steps.title: Follow the selected meaning
steps.query: How does it affect the nervous system?
steps.observe: The element interpretation persists and the returned passages discuss mercury exposure.

tours.title: Inspect and challenge the memory
tours.summary: Trace an earlier aspect, measure context sensitivity, and preview its removal without adding a turn.
tours.presenterNote: Context impact measures ranking sensitivity, not relevance improvement. The saved conversation must keep the same number of turns during previews.

steps.title: Establish a topic
steps.observe: The telescope subject is established.

steps.title: Introduce a specific aspect
steps.observe: Mirror becomes the current aspect.

steps.title: Carry that aspect forward
steps.observe: The trace includes an earlier aspect and its source turn.

steps.title: Compare context variants
steps.observe: Check context impact compares topic, earlier-aspect, and feedback removal using the same saved question.

steps.title: Preview without the earlier aspect
steps.observe: The ranking is recomputed without earlier aspect terms; the three saved turns remain unchanged.

steps.title: Restore the original context
steps.observe: The earlier mirror aspect returns in the preview.

tours.title: Teach the search, then undo
tours.summary: Pin evidence, add relevance feedback, reject a result, and reverse the correction.
tours.presenterNote: Feedback belongs to this topic. Pinning is an explicit user priority, not evidence that the passage is objectively relevant.

steps.title: Find candidate evidence
steps.observe: A ranked list provides evidence to annotate.

steps.title: Pin a lower-ranked passage
steps.observe: The selected passage moves to the top of a current-feedback preview.

steps.title: Mark the pinned evidence relevant
steps.observe: The topic now contains separate pin and relevance annotations.

steps.title: Reject another passage
steps.observe: The rejected passage disappears from this topic's ranking preview.

steps.title: Undo the rejection
steps.observe: The exclusion is reversed while the earlier pin and relevance annotation remain.

tours.title: Open the IR engine
tours.summary: Demonstrate positional phrase matching, four retrieval methods, postings, fusion, and profiling.
tours.presenterNote: Rankings and model scores have different scales. The method comparison shows actual top-five overlap; it does not claim one method always wins.

steps.title: Run a quoted phrase
steps.observe: Positional intersection reports matching passages for the quoted phrase.

steps.title: Compare retrieval methods
steps.observe: The inspector replays the same question through BM25, SMART cosine, semantic search, and Hybrid.

steps.title: Inspect novelty and timing
steps.observe: Point out new versus repeated passages, distinct articles, and the real latency breakdown.

tours.title: Control focus and diversity
tours.summary: Switch between soft topic preference, a hard title constraint, domain filtering, and diverse discovery.
tours.presenterNote: Hard lock may fall back when fewer than ten candidates remain; the inspector reports the applied rule. Diversity trades redundancy against relevance.

steps.title: Establish telescope context
steps.observe: Begin with an unrestricted, softly focused retrieval.

steps.title: Apply the hard topic lock
steps.observe: Inspect the eligible candidate count and whether the lock or its documented fallback was applied.

steps.title: Apply a domain filter
steps.observe: Every returned passage comes from Space and Physics.

steps.title: Explore varied evidence
steps.observe: The domain restriction is cleared and MMR changes the relevance/redundancy balance.

tours.title: Spend neural effort where it matters
tours.summary: Compare first-stage retrieval with fixed and adaptive cross-encoder reranking.
tours.presenterNote: The cross-encoder scores claim/query and passage pairs locally. Adaptive depth is based on retrieval agreement; show the actual scored count rather than promising a speedup.

steps.title: Retrieve without a second stage
steps.query: What instruments does the James Webb Space Telescope carry?
steps.observe: First-stage hybrid retrieval produces the initial evidence order.

steps.title: Run fixed-depth reranking
steps.observe: The trace shows how many candidates were scored and the local model timing.

steps.title: Run adaptive reranking
steps.observe: Inspect the chosen depth and a result's original rank and cross-encoder logit.

tours.title: Make the improvements visible
tours.summary: Inspect midterm versus final rankings, then retrieve separate evidence for two subjects.
tours.presenterNote: Compare ranking changes and source passages. Two-subject evidence is retrieved independently; it is not an automatically verified comparison answer.

steps.title: Establish the subject
steps.observe: Create context for the comparison.

steps.title: Save a contextual follow-up
steps.observe: The saved follow-up depends on the earlier telescope question.

steps.title: Compare midterm and final
steps.observe: Both engines receive the same earlier questions; inspect their passages and rank changes.

steps.title: Compare evidence for two telescopes
steps.observe: Read separate evidence columns for JWST and Hubble.

tours.title: Show measured results honestly
tours.summary: Replay a graded benchmark question and explain evaluation coverage and limitations.
tours.presenterNote: The inherited judgments are AI-derived, new results may be unjudged, and TEST was inspected during debugging. Synthetic checks and retrieval effectiveness answer different questions.

steps.title: Replay a graded conversation
steps.observe: Read the same benchmark question and earlier context in both engines, with known grades and unjudged coverage.

steps.title: Open the measured experiments
steps.observe: Inspect actual metrics, ablations, behavioral checks, and the blind review pool. Explain what remains unvalidated.

tours.title: Explore a word inside any question
tours.summary: Explore a term separately from the question, choose an indexed interpretation, and supply a custom focus.
tours.presenterNote: The explored word need not appear in the question. A custom focus is explicitly user-supplied retrieval context, not an automatically verified entity or fact.

steps.title: Explore a term for a separate question
steps.observe: Explore Transformer while preserving the original voltage question. The corpus offers electrical and neural interpretations.

steps.title: Choose the electrical article
steps.observe: The original question is searched using the selected indexed subject.

steps.title: Provide a custom focus
steps.observe: The user-defined label and keywords become visible retrieval context with real source passages.
